purpose: Visitor-selected, low-jargon specialist entrances that reuse existing public research/demo sources and share an evidence/consent contract without forcing a single universal identity.
source_of_truth: CoCivium currentness plus exact source hashes; this catalog is a public projection, not custody, authentication, a global registry, or proof of deployment.

lanes.label: Learn
lanes.audience_prompt: I want to understand a claim using real sources.

lanes.label: Play
lanes.audience_prompt: I want a playful way to test a coordination problem.
lanes.first_deed: Read one clearly fictional software spoof and describe one real coordination pain

lanes.label: Make
lanes.audience_prompt: I want to try one small, inspectable interface.
lanes.first_deed: Download and open the offline demo; test Preview, Reject, Accept, Undo

lanes.label: Explore
lanes.audience_prompt: I want to inspect claims and unknowns.
lanes.first_deed: Choose one CoOrb node and follow its source or uncertainty

aliases.dns: No new DNS/TLD/registration/redirect claims. Use descriptive paths under one qualified HTTPS root only after hosting audit.
aliases.dot_node_dot_clone: Symbolic type/name slots; not asserted globally delegated Internet TLDs
aliases.existing_app_game_domains: Externally owned namespace; no ability to use without registration/rights

shared_cross_surface_contract.privacy: No background profiling, contact harvesting, silent cross-lane tracking, account inference or cross-domain identity correlation
shared_cross_surface_contract.fallback: Source-linked static GitHub instructions, not another provider session

federation_policy.cooperate: Share portable consent, source evidence, accessibility, version/currentness and revocation contract, not user secrets.
federation_policy.compete: Run consented comparable 5-minute experiments with different explicit headlines and tasks; judge each on independent task completion, comprehension, reversibility and cost.

hypotheses.claim: Four plain-language task paths lower initial comprehension friction compared with research-heavy homepage.
hypotheses.test: Consent-based A/B comparison: version-pinned generic entry vs participant-selected path; independent observer records unaided comprehension and correct first click; no covert assignments or fingerprinting.

hypotheses.claim: A specialized entry increases completing one useful task.
hypotheses.test: Observe successful five-minute task completion and user-judged usefulness in a tiny consented cohort, separate visits from completions.

hypotheses.claim: Opt-in cross-lane links improve discovery without feeling like a firehose.
hypotheses.test: Compare no suggestion vs one visible optional cross-link; record acceptance, confusion, requests to stop; abort if friction grows.

hypotheses.claim: Shared provenance and identity boundaries survive transitions among lanes.
hypotheses.test: Same test object projected through two lanes retains its exact source ID, provenance and privacy scope; no receiver acknowledgment without a receiver receipt.
